title: 10. Exercises: Threading Patterns
objectives: Solve the Threading Patterns exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
### Exercise 1: Rate-Limited Producer

Create a producer-consumer where:

1. Producer generates items at max 10/second
2. Consumer processes items (0.2s each)
3. Buffer size is 5
4. Show backpressure effects

### Exercise 2: Priority Worker Pool

Extend the worker pool to:

1. Support task priorities
2. High priority tasks processed first
3. Report average wait time by priority

### Exercise 3: Cached Resource Pool

Create a connection pool that:

1. Has max 5 connections
2. Reuses connections (returns to pool)
3. Times out idle connections after 10s
4. Creates new connections on demand

### Exercise 4: Parallel Map-Reduce

Implement parallel map-reduce:

1. Map phase: transform items in parallel
2. Reduce phase: combine results
3. Test with: sum of squares of 1 to 1000

### Exercise 5: Fan-Out/Fan-In

Create a pattern where:

1. One producer generates work
2. Work is distributed to N workers
3. Results are collected by one aggregator
4. Final result is returned

### Exercise 6: Timeout Queue

Implement a queue where:

1. Items expire after N seconds
2. Expired items are automatically removed
3. get() never returns expired items
4. Report expiration statistics

### Exercise 7: Pipeline Pattern

Create a data processing pipeline:

1. Stage 1: Read data (I/O)
2. Stage 2: Parse data (CPU)
3. Stage 3: Validate data (CPU)
4. Stage 4: Save data (I/O)
   Each stage runs in parallel.

### Exercise 8: Bounded Thread Pool

Extend ThreadPoolExecutor to:

1. Queue only N pending tasks
2. Block submit() when queue full
3. Add submit_nowait() that raises if full
4. Report queue depth

### Exercise 9: Retry Pattern with Pool

Create a resilient worker that:

1. Retries failed tasks up to 3 times
2. Exponential backoff between retries
3. Dead letter queue for permanent failures
4. Reports success/retry/failure counts

### Exercise 10: Dynamic Worker Scaling

Create a worker pool that:

1. Starts with 2 workers
2. Scales up when queue > 10 items
3. Scales down when queue < 2 items (and workers > 2)
4. Max 10 workers
5. Log scaling events

**Next: [05_multiprocessing_basics.md](./05_multiprocessing_basics.md)** — Learn true parallel execution with processes →
